1934	\subsection{The inference of a call's static arguments}
1935	\seclabel{revival-inference}
1936	
1937	\begin{description}
1938	\item[Affected sections] \chapref{type-inference}; \secref{ranges};
1939	\secref{basic-integers}; \secref{revival-ranges}; \secref{revival-notrevised}.
1940	\item[Change] \chapref{type-inference}, which held a heading and two draft
1941	notes, states how the static arguments of a call that does not write them are
1942	inferred, for type parameters and for \KWD{nat} and \KWD{int} parameters.
1943	The declaration is chosen first, as \secref{resolving-coercion} chooses it, a
1944	declaration with static parameters being applicable to a call if some instance
1945	of it within its bounds is, and compared on the parameter types it declares.
1946	Its static arguments are then inferred: a type, \KWD{nat} or \KWD{int}
1947	parameter that a parameter type mentions inside another type is fixed by the
1948	argument, and a type parameter that the return type mentions inside another
1949	type by the expected type; a type parameter that
1950	is the whole type of parameters takes the narrowest type that their arguments
1951	are substitutable for, which for number arguments is the narrowest type into
1952	which every one of them converts, and otherwise, since 29~September 2026, its
1953	bound (below); every
1954	argument is admitted by substitutability, the coercions the instance needs are
1955	inserted statically, and the converted call dispatches by subtyping.
1956	A call written by tight juxtaposition, as a method invocation or as an operator
1957	application, has an expected type in the contexts the chapter lists, a variable
1958	or field declaration and an assignment to a variable among them, and is
1959	inferred again without it when its result then converts.
1960	A numeral whose conversions tie is read as a \EXP{\mathbb{Z}32}, or as a
1961	\EXP{\mathbb{Z}64} or a \EXP{\mathbb{Z}} by its value; any other tie among
1962	declarations applicable only with coercion is a static error.
1963	The chapter lists what it does not yet describe, the static arguments of a
1964	\KWD{bool}, \KWD{dim}, \KWD{unit} or operator parameter among them, keeps the
1965	second of the two draft notes, and has three boxes: on the Working Draft, the
1966	bound it assumes and the passages it leaves to the revision of the overloading
1967	chapters; on the interpreter; and on a type parameter that only the return
1968	type mentions and on the \KWD{bool} parameters that neither implementation
1969	infers.
1970	The ranges section says that a \KWD{nat} or \KWD{int} parameter used as a
1971	component converts to \EXP{\mathbb{Z}32} as an integer numeral does, with a
1972	box.
1973	The box in \secref{basic-integers} says that a generic call over two different
1974	integer types infers the narrowest type that both coerce into by the rule of
1975	\chapref{type-inference}.
1976	\secref{revival-notrevised} says that the rule is written and names the passages
1977	the chapter leaves unrevised, and it and the effect of \secref{revival-ranges}
1978	say that the question of a \KWD{nat} parameter in a range is settled.
1979	On 29~September 2026 one sentence of the rule changed.
1980	Of a type parameter that is the whole type of parameters, where no narrowest
1981	candidate exists and the rule for numerals does not settle the tie, the
1982	chapter said that it ``takes the union of the types of those arguments
1983	(\secref{internal-types}), if its bounds permit that, and none of those
1984	arguments is converted''; it now takes the intersection of its upper bounds,
1985	its declared bound, \TYP{Any} if it has none, and what the expected type
1986	requires of the declared return type, none of those arguments converted, with
1987	a box.
1988	With the revision of the overloading chapters (\secref{revival-overloading}),
1989	the first box points to this entry's list of the cases in which the compiled
1990	type checker departs from the chapter and no longer names the passages that revision revised, and the box

43	is self-contained and completely describes a set of integers.  Its

45	$a$, $b$, and $c$ are expressions that produce such values.
46	An integer numeral converts to \EXP{\mathbb{Z}32} (\secref{literals}), and a

52	(\secref{revival-ranges}) left open whether a \KWD{nat} parameter, which may

60	\begin{itemize}
61	\item The range \EXP{a\COLONOP{}b} is the set of $n=\max(0,b-a+1)$ integers $\{a, a+1, a+2, \ldots, b-2, b-1, b\}$.
62	This is a \emph{nonstrided} range.
63	If \VAR{a} and \VAR{b} are both static expressions
64	(described in \secref{static-expr}),
65	then it is a \emph{static range} of type \EXP{\TYP{StaticRange}\llbracket{}a,n,1\rrbracket}
66	and therefore also a \emph{range of static size} of type \EXP{\TYP{RangeOfStaticSize}\llbracket{}n\rrbracket}.
67	
68	\item The range \EXP{a\COLONOP{}b\COLONOP{}c} is
69	the set of $n=\max\left(0, \left\lfloor {b-a+c \over c} \right\rfloor \right)$ integers
70	$\{a, a+c, a+2c, \ldots, a + \left\lfloor {b-a \over c} \right\rfloor c\}$,
71	unless $c$ is zero, in which case it throws an exception.
72	(If $c$ is a static expression, then it is a static error if $c$ is zero.)
73	This is a \emph{strided} range.
74	If \VAR{a}, \VAR{b}, and \VAR{c} are all static expressions,
75	then it is a \emph{static range} of type \EXP{\TYP{StaticRange}\llbracket{}a,n,c\rrbracket}

18	\section{Changes Made by the 2026 Revival to the Working Draft}
19	\seclabel{revival-changes}
20	\sloppy
21	
22	This section lists the changes made to this working draft by the 2026
23	revival of the Fortress project (\url{https://github.com/palimondo/fortress}).
24	The revival works to finish what the designers intended, judged by this
25	working draft, and changes the text only where a decision it has taken for
26	the implementation would otherwise leave the text and the implementation in
27	open disagreement.
28	Each changed passage carries a box headed
29	``Revised by the 2026 revival'' that points to its entry here.
30	
31	Each entry gives the affected sections, the change, its rationale, its
32	effect, the original text, and what reversing to the alternative not taken
33	would require.
34	The original text is that of the \emph{Working Draft of February 2011},
35	the unrevised copy of this document kept in the revival's repository under
36	the directory \nolinkurl{Specification-1.0-frozen/}, cited by path and line
37	there.
38	The directory's name is misleading: its sources are the working draft of
39	2~February 2011, and only the file \nolinkurl{fortress.1.0.pdf} in it is the
40	Fortress~1.0 release.
41	The full reasoning behind every entry, with each original passage and each
42	new one, is in the revival's decision records,
43	\nolinkurl{explorations/compile-ladder/rung-spec-route-a/decision-record.md}
44	and, for the number chapters,
45	\nolinkurl{explorations/compile-ladder/rung-spec-numbers/decision-record.md},
46	in the same repository.
47	
48	Each change below follows a decision of the revival.
49	The first of those decisions, taken on
50	24~September 2026 and called \emph{route~A}, is that the compiled type checker keeps
51	the type group's rule that no type is a subtype of two different
52	instantiations of one parameterized trait, a rule this working draft never
53	stated, and that the library's numeric types are reorganized so that they
54	satisfy it.
55	An entry whose change does not follow from route~A says so, and names the
56	decision it follows or gives its reason.
57	The revision of the number chapters (\secref{revival-numbers} to
58	\secref{revival-reductions}) also carries out three decisions of
59	26~September 2026 that follow from route~A: on the refined number types, on
60	conversions between number types, and on sums and products.
61	The alternative not taken, \emph{route~C}, is described once, in
62	\secref{revival-routec}.
63	
64	\subsection{Instantiation exclusion}

<!-- Judgement of the curator's numeral design of 2026-11-08 (machine defaults where no type is declared; the Working Draft's numeral types as fields; a program's type coerces from the numeral type once at load), for the coordinator, before it goes to POSITIONS and a batch. Sources: the brief, the Working Draft (`Specification-1.0-frozen/`), the record, the three reviews and the prototype of 2026-11-08. -->

# Judgement: the numeral design of 2026-11-08

## 2. Against the record

- Revised: P-76 (the name; "walk's half" once walk has static types, which the default makes walk's rule today; `IntLiteral`'s arithmetic, which the fold retires). P-172: the name; "Where nothing fixes a type ... the numeral stays an exact `FloatLiteral`: `Cell(0.5)` is a `Cell[\FloatLiteral\]`"; "prints a bare numeral as written, as the team's `tests/NumberPrintTest.fss:16` asserts", a team test that now breaks; its two open items close.
- Facts: F-79, F-57 (the checker's two types), F-169 (the text's `IntLiteral`), F-73 (the tie reading becomes the rule, floats included), F-74 (walk's numeral by value, a gap made the rule), F-118, F-262. P-169: the 24 numeral glue bindings and their carrier fall away (probe §4.5).
- Bent: P-26. The prelude keeps the numeral's type at every untyped place (fork §3.3), code "built alike for all its types"; the Draft's types are unfinished text (F-169), the names the implementers' later word. No team word calls them temporary (scout §10). The one team word for point 4: "IntLiterals should always be transient objects with minimal lifetime" (`compiler/runtimeValues/FIntLiteral.java:21-23`, 2009). The entry should own the weighing as the curator's.
- Unchanged: P-168, P-171, P-165 (a name only), P-49, P-46, P-40, P-74.

## 4. The sub-choices

- `=` pairs stay and fold: follows from P-165 with point 1; without them `u = 0` for `u: NN32`, `NN64`, `RR32` falls to `SEQV`, `false` (probe §5, §9). "Fold" means: the pair's conversion of its numeral runs at compile time, as at any typed place.
- `gg(5, w)` takes the `ZZ32` declaration: follows from point 1 with P-49. Flips `InferO2Pos:18-19` and `inference.tex:186`.
- `x = 7/2` a `QQ`, a comparison of literals folds: conflicts with point 5 as prototyped (`7/2` → `RR64`, decision 4); coherent with repair 3, after which `1/2 = 0.5` is `true` through the kept pair and the comparison need not fold. The Draft (`:163-166`, a rational static expression), the restart and the library's `/` favour `QQ`.
- A numeral type written only as a coercion's or operator's parameter type: follows from point 4; must also cover inferred types (repair 2). Breaks 9 team and 10 revival tests that write `IntLiteral` (probe §4.3): a point to report.
- An expression of numerals folds exactly: free. The alternative, numeral types with no arithmetic, makes `3 + 4` `ZZ32` arithmetic and `2147483647 + 1` an overflow. The Draft (`:165-173`) and P-171's string fold favour the fold; it needs repair 3 and the prototype's exceptions (`-0.0`, `1/0`; decision 5).
- Strings: P-171, decided; independent of points 1 to 4.

## 5. The test cases

The appendix lists 42 programs with the design's answer, today's, and a mark: [P] the prototype measured it, [W] a review on walk, [R] by reading. Those that separate it from today: `x SEQV z` and `Cell(3)`, where the paths first agree; `"" 2.50` and `NumberPrintTest:16`, printing the double; `q: QQ = y` refused for `y = 0.1`; `g(bigN)` (row 946 closes); `z: ZZ32 = 3000000000`, static where the prototype left it at run time; the own-type cases; `C.8_16` round-tripped, which no path gives; microGPT, no line and no bit changed, by reading only (probe §4.7).

## 6. Open for the curator

- Out-of-range at a typed place: static (point 2) or run-time (the prototype).
- A program's type with no coercion from the numeral type: refused, or default then coerce.
- "Once per class": one object per site as a rule, or value types only.
- A `nat` used as a value: `NN32` (the Draft) or `ZZ32` (P-40).
- The fold's result: a signed constant with three defaults, or the Draft's constant traits.
- A numeral-typed value inside a coercion's body: bindable by inference, or only the parameter.
- `NumberPrintTest:16` and the 9 team tests writing `IntLiteral`: respelled, or kept red.
- `SEQV` of two numeral values: by fields (P-168) or by reduced value (probe §7.1).
- Walk before P-12: the float numeral defaults at evaluation (F-c) or converts place by place.
- The binary chapter's `||` with a numeral, and `constant.tex:84-87`'s numeral `||`: dropped, folded, or given a written size.

\chapter{Numbers}
\chaplabel{lib:numbers-basic}


\section{Rational Numbers}
\seclabel{basic-rationals}

The trait \EXP{\mathbb{Q}} (\STR{QQ}) encompasses all finite rational numbers,
the results of dividing any integer by any nonzero integer.
The trait \EXP{\mathbb{Q}^*} (\STR{QQ{\char'137}star}) is \EXP{\mathbb{Q}} with
two extra elements, \EXP{+\infty} and \EXP{-\infty}.
The trait \EXP{\mathbb{Q}^{\#}} (\STR{QQ{\char'137}splat}) is \EXP{\mathbb{Q}^*} with
one additional element, the indefinite rational (written \EXP{0/0}), which is used as the result
of dividing zero by zero or of adding \EXP{-\infty} to \EXP{+\infty}.

Often it is desirable to indicate that a variable ranges over only a subset of
the rationals, such as only positive values or only nonnegative values or only
nonzero values.
Unfortunately, traditional notations such as \EXP{\mathbb{Q}^+} are not used consistently
in the literature; one author may use \EXP{\mathbb{Q}^+} to mean the set of strictly positive rationals
and another may use it to mean the set of nonnegative rationals.
Fortress therefore uses a notation that is novel but unambiguous:

\begin{tabbing}
\EXP{\mathbb{Q}} (\STR{QQ}) is the set of rationals
(it is a subtype of \EXP{\mathbb{R}} and \EXP{\mathbb{Q}^*}).
\\
\EXP{\mathbb{Q}_{<}} (\STR{QQ{\char'137}LT}) is the set of strictly negative rationals
(it is a subtype of \EXP{\mathbb{R}_{<}}, \EXP{\mathbb{Q}^*_{<}}, \EXP{\mathbb{Q}}, \EXP{\mathbb{Q}_{\leq}}, and \EXP{\mathbb{Q}_{\neq}}).
\\
\EXP{\mathbb{Q}_{\leq}} (\STR{QQ{\char'137}LE}) is the set of nonpositive rationals, that is, \EXP{\mathbb{Q}_{<} \cup \{0\}}
(it is a subtype of \EXP{\mathbb{R}_{\leq}}, \EXP{\mathbb{Q}^*_{\leq}}, and \EXP{\mathbb{Q}}).
\\
\EXP{\mathbb{Q}_{\geq}} (\STR{QQ{\char'137}GE}) is the set of nonnegative rationals, that is, \EXP{\mathbb{Q}_{>} \cup \{0\}}
(it is a subtype of \EXP{\mathbb{R}_{\geq}}, \EXP{\mathbb{Q}^*_{\geq}}, and \EXP{\mathbb{Q}}).
\\
\EXP{\mathbb{Q}_{>}} (\STR{QQ{\char'137}GT}) is the set of strictly positive rationals
(it is a subtype of \EXP{\mathbb{R}_{>}}, \EXP{\mathbb{Q}^*_{>}}, \EXP{\mathbb{Q}}, \EXP{\mathbb{Q}_{\geq}}, and \EXP{\mathbb{Q}_{\neq}}).
\\
\EXP{\mathbb{Q}_{\neq}} (\STR{QQ{\char'137}NE}) is the set of strictly nonzero rationals (that is, \EXP{\mathbb{Q}_{<} \cup \mathbb{Q}_{>}})
(it is a subtype of \EXP{\mathbb{R}_{\neq}}, \EXP{\mathbb{Q}^*_{\neq}}, and \EXP{\mathbb{Q}}).
\\
\EXP{\mathbb{Q}^*} (\STR{QQ{\char'137}star}) is \EXP{\mathbb{Q}} with extra elements \EXP{+\infty} and \EXP{-\infty}
(it is a subtype of \EXP{\mathbb{R}^*} and \EXP{\mathbb{Q}^{\#}}).
\\
\EXP{\mathbb{Q}^*_{<}} (\STR{QQ{\char'137}star{\char'137}LT}) is \EXP{\mathbb{Q}_{<}} with extra element \EXP{-\infty}
(it is a subtype of \EXP{\mathbb{R}^*_{<}}, \EXP{\mathbb{Q}^{\#}_{<}}, \EXP{\mathbb{Q}^*}, \EXP{\mathbb{Q}^*_{\leq}}, and \EXP{\mathbb{Q}^*_{\neq}}).
\\
\EXP{\mathbb{Q}^*_{\leq}} (\STR{QQ{\char'137}star{\char'137}LE}) is \EXP{\mathbb{Q}_{\leq}} with extra element \EXP{-\infty}

p = 'Specification/advanced-lib/binary.tex'
L = open(p, encoding='utf-8').read().split('\n')
OPR = r"""\revision{revival-numerals}{The two operators \EXP{\|} above whose other
operand is a \TYP{NaturalNumeral} take the numeral's digit count, radix and
value as static parameters.
The revival's numeral types have no static parameters: the four numbers of a
numeral are fields of its value (\secref{literals}), and a field cannot give a
static size, so no library can declare these operators as written, and a
concatenation with a numeral has no static result type.
The declarations stand as the Working Draft gives them.}"""
COE = r"""\revision{revival-numerals}{The coercion above from a \TYP{NaturalNumeral}
takes the numeral's digit count, radix and value as static parameters.
The revival's numeral types have no static parameters: the four numbers of a
numeral are fields of its value (\secref{literals}).
A coercion from \TYP{NaturalNumeral} into a sequence of a written size can read
the radix and the digit count when it is applied, and throw where they do not
fit, but it cannot take a size from the digit count as a static size.
The declaration stands as the Working Draft gives it.}"""
BOTH = r"""\revision{revival-numerals}{The coercion and the two operators \EXP{\|}
above whose parameter is a \TYP{NaturalNumeral} take the numeral's digit count,
radix and value as static parameters.
The revival's numeral types have no static parameters: the four numbers of a
numeral are fields of its value (\secref{literals}), and a field cannot give a
static size.
So no library can declare them as written: a coercion from
\TYP{NaturalNumeral} into a sequence of a written size can read the radix and
the digit count when it is applied, but not take a size from them, and a
concatenation with a numeral has no static result type.
The declarations stand as the Working Draft gives them.}"""
ins = {924: OPR, 1137: OPR, 1735: BOTH, 1753: COE, 1871: OPR, 2099: BOTH, 2117: COE, 2285: OPR}
expect = {924: r'\end{Fortress}', 2099: r'\end{Fortress}', 1735: r'\end{Fortress}'}
for ln in sorted(ins, reverse=True):
    cur = L[ln-1]
    want = expect.get(ln, '[Description to be supplied.]')
    assert cur == want, (ln, cur)
    L[ln:ln] = ins[ln].split('\n')
open(p, 'w', encoding='utf-8').write('\n'.join(L))
print('inserted', len(ins))
EOF

126	
127	Coercion is \emph{not} automatically chained in Fortress, unlike some
128	other programming languages: even if type \VAR{T} can be coerced to
129	type \VAR{U} and type \VAR{U} can be coerced to type \VAR{V}, it is
130	not necessarily the case that type \VAR{T} can be coerced to type
131	\VAR{V}.  Type \VAR{T} can be coerced to type \VAR{V} only if this
132	coercion is explicitly defined.
36	and static expressions:
37	\begin{enumerate}
38	\item The \emph{literal} traits, which describe boolean,
39	  character, string, and numerals.  For example, the literal \VAR{true} has
40	  trait \EXP{\TYP{BooleanLiteral}\llbracket\VAR{true}\rrbracket} and a
41	  character literal has trait \TYP{Character}.
42	See \secref{literals} for a discussion of Fortress literals.
43	
44	\item The \emph{constant} traits, which describe values denoted by
45	expressions composed from literals and operators (described in
46	\secref{constant-values});
47	the type of a constant expression encodes the value of the expression.
48	For example, the type of a constant expression \EXP{3+5},
49	%IntegerConstant[\false, 3+5\]
50	\EXP{\TYP{IntegerConstant}\llbracket\VAR{false}, 3+5\rrbracket},
51	encodes the value of the expression; the operator \EXP{+} is
52	used in the static arguments.  When an operator is not supported in static
53	arguments, \library\ can still encode the value of the expression by
54	providing a specific constant trait such as
55	\EXP{\TYP{RationalValueTimesPi}\llbracket\VAR{false},1,1\rrbracket}
56	(described in \secref{pi}).
74	
75	The only operation on literals that produces a new literal (as opposed
76	to a constant) is concatenation by using the operator \EXP{\|}.
77	One may concatenate mixed string and
78	character literals, producing a string literal.
79	For example, ``\txt{foo}''\EXP{\|}''\txt{bar}'' yields ``\txt{foobar}''.
80	One may also concatenate two natural numerals
81	of the same radix, producing a new natural numeral of that radix.
82	For example, \EXP{\mathtt{deadc}_{16} \| \mathtt{0de}_{16}} yields \EXP{\mathtt{deadc0de}_{16}}.

\subsection{The numeral types, their conversion and their default}
\seclabel{revival-numerals}

\begin{description}
\item[Affected sections] \secref{literals}; \secref{static-expr};
\secref{coercion}; \secref{static-arg-inference}; \secref{numeral-default};
\secref{basic-rationals}; \secref{natparams}; \secref{lib:BinaryEndianWord};
\secref{lib:BinaryLinearEndianSequence};
\secref{lib:BinaryEndianLinearEndianSequence}; \secref{revival-numeral-type};
\secref{revival-inference}; \secref{revival-asfloat};
\secref{revival-object-kinds}.
\item[Change] \secref{literals} says that every numeral has the type
\TYP{Numeral}, through \TYP{NaturalNumeral} for a numeral without a radix point
or \TYP{RadixPointNumeral} for one with a radix point, and that its value holds
the four numbers that were the static arguments of the Working Draft's numeral
types, its digit count $n$, the number $m$ of its digits after the radix point,
its radix $r$ and the value $v$ of its digits, as the getters \VAR{digits},
\VAR{fractionDigits}, \VAR{radix} and \VAR{digitValue}; the two types with an
explicit radix fold into the radix, and \TYP{Literal} into the digit count.
Its paragraph that said that numerals are not directly converted now says that a
numeral is converted where it stands, and its sentences on library designers
and their coercions stand.
New paragraphs say where a place fixes a type: where the type declared there
declares a coercion from the numeral's type or is a numeral type; that there
the numeral is converted from its exact value, exactly into the integer types
and \EXP{\mathbb{Q}} and with one rounding into \EXP{\mathbb{R}64} and
\EXP{\mathbb{R}32}, a numeral outside the type's range being a static error;
that elsewhere it is converted into its default, \EXP{\mathbb{Z}32},
\EXP{\mathbb{Z}64} or \EXP{\mathbb{Z}} by its value, or \EXP{\mathbb{R}64} with
a radix point, the default applying to a numeral and never to an expression of
a numeral type; that a type of a program's own receives a numeral only through
its coercion from the numeral's type, which sees the four numbers of a numeral
as written and is applied once for each place, so that the place denotes one
object; that a numeral type is written only as a parameter type; and that
inside a coercion's body two numeral values are equal and strictly equivalent
by their value.
Its box on the numeral's type is rewritten, and two boxes are added, after the
numeral types and after the paragraph on static rational expressions.
\secref{static-expr} says, after its list of the traits of static expressions,
that \library\ declare no constant trait and that an expression of numerals and
operators is folded exactly into a signed constant, which takes one of three
defaults where nothing fixes its type, and which operators it leaves alone; a
box follows, and another follows the paragraph on the concatenation of literals,
which says that the concatenation of two natural numerals is built.
\secref{coercion} says that a numeral's conversion into its default is a rule
beside coercion, that a numeral is applicable without coercion to a parameter of
its default type and to one that fixes no type, and that a type of a program's
own without a coercion from the numeral's type refuses a numeral, with a box;
its box on integers in floating-point expressions names the type
\TYP{NaturalNumeral}, and no longer says that the interpreter leaves a large
numeral unconverted.
\secref{static-arg-inference} says that \EXP{\VAR{id}(3)} is instantiated at the
numeral's default, with a box.
\secref{numeral-default} gives the default at every place that fixes no type,
the narrowest default for a type parameter or the branches that several
numerals fix, and the tie of a numeral with a radix point read as an
\EXP{\mathbb{R}64}, with a box.
\secref{basic-rationals} names the coercions from the two numeral types, their
pairs of \EXP{=} and their \VAR{asFloat}, with a box.
\secref{natparams} gains a box on a \KWD{nat} parameter used as a value, and
the binary chapter's declarations over \TYP{NaturalNumeral} gain eight boxes;
the text of both stands.
The entries \secref{revival-numeral-type}, \secref{revival-inference},
\secref{revival-asfloat} and \secref{revival-object-kinds} are revised where
they named \TYP{IntLiteral} or said what the interpreter does with a numeral.
\item[Rationale] This change does not follow from route~A.
The revival decided on 8~November 2026 that a numeral is converted where it
stands, into the type that its place fixes or else into the machine default;
that its own type is the Working Draft's \TYP{NaturalNumeral} or
\TYP{RadixPointNumeral}, below \TYP{Numeral}, the four numbers fields of its
value; and that a type of a program's own receives a numeral through its
coercion from that type, which the compiled code applies once for each place.
The Working Draft gives numerals types of their own so that library designers
decide by coercions how numerals meet other types, and so that an interval type
receives \EXP{3.1415926535897932384} unrounded
(\nolinkurl{Specification-1.0-frozen/basic/expressions/literals.tex}, lines
132--148).
The team built that coercion under its own names, with the numeral's exact
value, in the compiled path's own library (``ZZ32 now coerces IntLiteral as
described in the spec'', the team's commit \texttt{128f313b5b} of 17~November
2009, in the revival's repository), but never the four numbers.
The change keeps what the team built, one type for each kind of numeral with
its exact value at the coercion, and adds the Working Draft's names and
numbers: a coercion that receives only a floating-point value rounds twice, as a
16-bit floating-point type of a program's own would round
\EXP{1.00390625000000000001} first to the nearest \EXP{\mathbb{R}64} and then to
a 16-bit value other than the one nearest to the numeral.
A field cannot give a static size, so the binary chapter's static word width
from a numeral's digit count cannot be declared, and its \EXP{\|} with a numeral
has no static result type; those declarations stand, each with a box.
The default is the type that the interpreter already gave an integer numeral by
its value, and the Java programming language's type for an integer literal.
The revival declined exact defaults, \EXP{\mathbb{Z}} and \EXP{\mathbb{Q}}, as
the team's restart of 2012 gives \EXP{\mathbb{N}} and \EXP{\mathbb{Q}}
(\nolinkurl{Documentation/Specification/Prose/Language/Expressions/literals.tick},
line 25), since its model program's constants declared without a type would then
be rationals and every index declared without a type would need a conversion.
In two places the change departs from the revival's rule that the team's later
decision wins over its earlier one: the compiled path's own library, the team's
later word, names its numeral types \TYP{IntLiteral} and \TYP{FloatLiteral}, and
keeps a numeral's own type at every place that fixes no type.
The revival takes the Working Draft's names and the default as its own
finishing of the text; no source of the team calls those names either final or
temporary.
The team's one word on a numeral's value at run time, that ``IntLiterals should
always be transient objects with minimal lifetime''
(\nolinkurl{ProjectFortress/src/com/sun/fortress/compiler/runtimeValues/FIntLiteral.java},
lines 21--23), is kept: a program meets a numeral's value only inside a
coercion or an operator whose parameter has a numeral type.
An expression of numerals alone is folded exactly, as the Working Draft computes
a static rational expression exactly and rounds it at most once
(\nolinkurl{Specification-1.0-frozen/basic/expressions/literals.tex}, lines
162--173); its result is a signed constant written as numerals, not a value of a
constant trait, so that a coercion of a program's own sees only the four numbers
of a numeral as written, and \EXP{x = 7/2} stays a rational.
A \KWD{nat} parameter used as a value has one type, \EXP{\mathbb{Z}32}, as the
revival decided on 28~September 2026 for the ranges (\secref{revival-inference}),
not \EXP{\mathbb{N}32} as \secref{natparams} says.
A numeral at a type of a program's own that declares no coercion from the
numeral's type is refused, since coercion does not chain; the alternative not
taken converts it into its default first and then by the type's own coercion
from that default.
A reversal to the Working Draft's polymorphic numerals would keep a numeral's
own type wherever nothing fixes a type, as the compiled path's own library does,
so that \EXP{x = 3} binds a numeral and \EXP{\TYP{Cell}(3)} is a
\EXP{\TYP{Cell}\llbracket\TYP{NaturalNumeral}\rrbracket}; a reversal to the names
of \secref{revival-numeral-type} would rename the two types \TYP{IntLiteral} and
\TYP{FloatLiteral}, which no program that does not write them would notice.
The full reasoning is in
\nolinkurl{explorations/reviews/literal-design-judgement-2026-11-08.md} and
\nolinkurl{explorations/compile-ladder/rung-literals-spec/REPORT.md} in the
revival's repository.

type and give it its default elsewhere.
So \EXP{x = 3} binds a \EXP{\mathbb{Z}32}, and \EXP{x \sequiv z} is \VAR{true}

computed \EXP{0.25 + 0.25}, \EXP{q\COLON\mathbb{Q} = 0.5} binds \EXP{1/2}, and

(rows~943 and~944 of the revival's gap ledger); a variable of type
\EXP{\mathbb{N}32} or \EXP{\mathbb{N}64} takes a numeral, and one of type
\EXP{\mathbb{R}32} takes a numeral with one rounding, where the interpreter
refused them (row~454); a variable bound from \EXP{3000000000} is a
\EXP{\mathbb{Z}64} and reaches a declaration over \EXP{\mathbb{Z}64}, where the
compiled path stopped at run time (row~946); \EXP{7} passed to a parameter of
type \TYP{Object} is a \EXP{\mathbb{Z}32} there (row~79); a numeral outside its
type's range is a static error, where the compiled path raised an exception at
run time (row~325); a numeral at a declared floating-point type is rounded once,
where the compiled code rounded it two or three times (row~862); and a
\KWD{nat} parameter used as a value is a \EXP{\mathbb{Z}32}, which a variable of
type \EXP{\mathbb{N}32} refuses, where the compiled type checker took it
(row~486).
\EXP{\VAR{round}(2.50000000000000001)} is 2, its numeral read as an
\EXP{\mathbb{R}64}.
A numeral that took its default prints as a value of its default type, so that

\nolinkurl{ProjectFortress/tests/NumberPrintTest.fss}, which asserted that a
numeral prints as written, is changed; a value of a numeral type prints as the

class that holds the place is loaded, so that a coercion that throws an

No line of the revival's model program changes, and by reading none of its
numerals changes its value.

\subsection{A string literal as one object}
\seclabel{revival-string-literals}

\begin{description}
\item[Affected sections] \secref{literals}; \chapref{objects};
\secref{static-expr}; \secref{revival-object-kinds}.
\item[Change] \secref{literals} says that two string literals of the same text
denote one object, so that every evaluation of a string literal with a given
text yields the same string; that a string that a program builds as it runs is
another object than a literal of the same text, unless the operation that builds
it answers an existing string; and that a concatenation of string literals is a
string literal.
The opening of \chapref{objects} says the same of strict equivalence.
Each passage gains a box, and so does the paragraph of \secref{static-expr} on
the concatenation of literals, which says that it is built.
The effect of \secref{revival-object-kinds} gains a sentence.
\item[Rationale] This change does not follow from route~A; the revival decided
on 8~November 2026 that two string literals of one text are one object, on both
implementations, and that a concatenation of two string literals is folded into
one literal.
Strings remain reference objects, whose equality of text is their own \EXP{=}
(\secref{revival-object-kinds}).
Every source of the team that speaks of literals makes equal literals one value:
the Working Draft's ``Literals are values; they do not require evaluation''
(\nolinkurl{Specification-1.0-frozen/basic/expressions/literals.tex}, lines
25--26); the team's restart of 2012, ``All literals represent value objects''
(\nolinkurl{Documentation/Specification/Prose/Language/Expressions/literals.tick},
line 29); and the team's compiled test
\nolinkurl{ProjectFortress/compiler_regressions/seqv.fss}, line 22, which
expects \hbox{\rm``\STR{cat}''} to be strictly equivalent to
\hbox{\rm``\STR{cat}''}.
Java, Kotlin, Scala and Clojure, whose strings are Java strings, give equal
literals one object.
The concatenation is the Working Draft's own sentence, which neither of the
team's implementations built.
A reversal would have each evaluation of a string literal construct a new
string, so that two literals of one text are never strictly equivalent, and
would leave a concatenation of literals to be computed when it is evaluated.
The full reasoning is in \nolinkurl{explorations/reviews/literals-2026-11-08.md},
sections 6.1 and 6.4, in the revival's repository.
\item[Effect] On both implementations
\EXP{\hbox{\rm``\STR{ab}''} \sequiv \hbox{\rm``\STR{ab}''}} is \VAR{true}, as
is one literal evaluated twice, and so are
\EXP{(\hbox{\rm``\STR{foo}''} \| \hbox{\rm``\STR{bar}''}) \sequiv \hbox{\rm``\STR{foobar}''}}
and \EXP{(\hbox{\rm``\STR{a}''} \| \hbox{\rm`\STR{b}'}) \sequiv \hbox{\rm``\STR{ab}''}},
where both answered \VAR{false} (row~945 of the revival's gap ledger).
A string built at run time is not strictly equivalent to an equal literal,
unless the library's operation answers the string it was given, as a substring
that spans its whole string does on both implementations.
The literals of \library\ are strings of this kind too, so that an empty
substring, which \library\ answer with their literal \hbox{\rm``''}, is strictly
equivalent to \hbox{\rm``''}.
The interpreter interns the text of each literal, and compares two flat strings
strictly by the identity of the Java strings that they carry; the compiled code
loads each literal as the Java Virtual Machine's interned string, and its strict
equivalence compares the Java strings that two of its string values carry by
identity.
The concatenation is folded in the desugaring that both implementations run
before the static check.
The compiled path's own library, until \library\ replace it, answers its own
\EXP{\sequiv} on two strings by their text (row~908).
\item[Original text] None: the Working Draft does not say whether two string
literals of the same text are one object.
The passages that this change builds stand, in
\nolinkurl{Specification-1.0-frozen/basic/expressions/literals.tex}, line 57,
``A string literal has type \TYP{String}.'', and in
\nolinkurl{Specification-1.0-frozen/basic/expressions/constant.tex}, lines
75--79:
\begin{quote}
The only operation on literals that produces a new literal (as opposed
to a constant) is concatenation by using the operator \EXP{\|}.
One may concatenate mixed string and
character literals, producing a string literal.
For example, ``\txt{foo}''\EXP{\|}''\txt{bar}'' yields ``\txt{foobar}''.
\end{quote}
\item[Route C] The same under route~C.
\end{description}

== explorations/fortress-gap-ledger.md:7-27

## The row template

A row is one line of eight cells, `| # | claim | status | class | spec citation | reproducer | found by | notes / workaround |`, at most 1,200 characters, in the table of its topic section, in number order. A pipe inside a cell is written `\|`. (POSITIONS, "The gap ledger's form"; the proposal behind it is `explorations/coordinator/process-engineering/gap-ledger-archaeology.md`, section 4.)

- **#**: the row's number, the next free one when it is added; never reused, renumbered or given to another row. 148 is vacant.
- **claim**: at most 300 characters, whose first 150 name the defect or the capability: what fails or what holds, and where.
- **status**: exactly one word of seven, with no second status and nothing in brackets:
  - `POSITIVE-VERIFIED`: it works; it ran and its output is recorded.
  - `NEGATIVE-VERIFIED`: the specification settles it and the reproducer confirms it. A row with one half fixed stays `NEGATIVE-VERIFIED`, and its notes say which half is fixed.
  - `NEGATIVE-BOUNDED`: the failure reproduces; the mechanisms tried are named and are not exhaustive.
  - `CONTESTED`: unsettled; the notes say why.
  - `RETIRED`: a source's claim falsified here, kept so that it is not derived again.
  - `FIXED`: closed by a landed commit (`ledger.py close`): the claim's first sentence, the test as reproducer, notes `fixed HASH; full text: history, row N`.
  - `DUPLICATE`: a pointer (`ledger.py duplicate`), notes `duplicate of row M; full text: history, row N`.
- **class**: `kind (area)`; `—` only for `POSITIVE-VERIFIED` and `RETIRED`. The kind is one of `implementation gap`, `library gap vs spec`, `library bug`, `design limit`, `deliberate`, `typesetter`, `packaging`; the area one of `parser`, `walk`, `checker`, `codegen`, `runtime`, `library`, `prelude`, `specification`, `tests`, `tools`.
- **spec citation**: the `.tex` file and the section heading in quotes, as `basic/operators/juxtameaning.tex`, "Juxtaposition"; a line number only against `Specification-1.0-frozen/`; `silent` where the specification does not say.
- **reproducer**: one test (its name, or its path under the test folders; an `XXX` test while it is an expected failure) or one probe path from the repository root, at most 200 characters; `none` when nothing in the tree reproduces it, with the command and its output, or the probe's old path, in the notes.
- **found by**: the stream that found it (`climb batch 8 rung I`, `run-c3`, `apl rung 2`), at most 60 characters; no date and no role.
- **notes / workaround**: at most 700 characters: `siblings: N, M` first if there are any; the mechanism, with file:line and the commit it was true at; the workaround; for a closed row, `fixed HASH`.

A path under `explorations/` that is no longer in the tree is read from history: `git show $(git log -1 --diff-filter=D --format=%h -- PATH)^:PATH`.

no static parameters. So 3.125 is a RadixPointNumeral whose four numbers are 4, 3, 10 and 3125, and 007 a
                           NaturalNumeral whose four numbers are 3, 0, 10 and 7.

                             D RAFT NOTE
                             Can the type NaturalNumeralJn, 10, vK have any value other than what you get from evaluating the corresponding
                             literal?

                             What is the relationship between LiteralJvK and NaturalNumeralJn, 10, vK ?

                             We need to describe the Numeral type hierarchy. All the numeric/numeral types should be defined and their
                             relations to each other given. And a reference to where that is done should be appear in this section (probably at
                             the beginning of the section).



                                                                                        124
   D RAFT NOTE
  Ought we discuss digit-group separators here? Or is that just part of lexical structure? (I think we intend that a
  numeral consisting of digits and digit-group separators has type NaturalNumeralJn, 10, vK for appropriate values
  of n and v .)


The radix of a numeral is ten, unless its digits are followed by an underscore and a radix indicator (Section 4.13), which
give its radix r; such a numeral has the same type as one without an indicator. So deadc16 is a NaturalNumeral
whose four numbers are 5, 0, 16 and 912092.

  R EVISED BY THE 2026 REVIVAL   SEE Section I.1.50

  The Working Draft of February 2011 gave a numeral the types NaturalNumeralJn, 10, vK , NaturalNumeralWithExplicitRadixJn, r, vK ,
  RadixPointNumeralJn, m, 10, vK , RadixPointNumeralWithExplicitRadixJn, m, r, vK , LiteralJvK for a numeral with-
  out leading zeros, and NumeralJn, m, r, vK , whose static arguments are the four numbers. The revival decided on 8 Novem-
  ber 2026 that the four numbers are fields of the numeral’s value: the two types with an explicit radix fold into the radix, and
  Literal into the digit count, which tells whether a numeral has leading zeros. So the team’s draft notes above are answered:
  two numerals of one kind have one type, which holds every such numeral, and Numeral comprises the two numeral types.


A numeral is converted where it stands, into the type that its place fixes, and not before, because, as in common mathe-
matical usage, we expect numerals to be polymorphic. For example, consider the numeral 3.1415926535897932384 ;
converting it to a floating-point number before its place is known may lose precision. If that numeral is used where
a floating-point interval is expected, it is better to convert it directly to an interval. Therefore, numerals have their
own types as described above. This approach allows library designers to decide how numerals should interact with
other types of objects by defining coercion operations (see Section 17.1 for an explanation of coercion in Fortress).
The Fortress standard libraries define coercions from numerals to integers (for simple numerals) and rational numbers
(for compound numerals). In the Fortress standard libraries, each of the eight number types (Section 33.1) declares a
coercion from NaturalNumeral, and Q , R64 and R32 declare one from RadixPointNumeral; the conversion is
exact into the five integer types (Section 33.2) and Q , and rounds once, to the nearest value of the type, into R64 and
R32 .
A place fixes a type for a numeral when the type declared there declares a coercion from the numeral’s type, as each
number type of the Fortress standard libraries does and a type of a program’s own may, or is a numeral type itself.
The declared type of a variable, a field or a parameter, and the declared return type of a functional, are such places,
the parameter types of the declaration that a call invokes among them (Section 17.5). There the numeral is converted
into that type, from its exact value: so q: Q = 0.1 binds the rational 1/10 , r: R64 = 0.1 the floating-point number
nearest to it, and n: N32 = 5 the natural number 5. It is a static error if the numeral’s value lies outside the range of
that type, or rounds to an infinity there. Where nothing fixes a type, as where a variable is declared without a type,
or a parameter has the type Any, Object or Number or a type parameter declared without a bound, the numeral is
converted into its default: a numeral without a radix point into Z32 , or into Z64 or Z when its value does not fit in the
narrower type, and a numeral with a radix point into R64 . So x = 3 binds x as a Z32 , bigN = 3000000000 binds
bigN as a Z64 and y = 0.5 binds y as an R64 ; x ≡ z is true for z: Z32 = 3 ; and for object CellJT K(x: T ) ,
Cell(3) is a CellJZ32K . Section 20.2 says where else a numeral takes its default, as where several numerals fix one
type parameter, and how a numeral whose conversions tie is read. The default applies to a numeral, and to a static
expression of numerals once it is folded (Section 13.27), never to an expression of a numeral type.
A type of a program’s own receives a numeral through its own coercion from the numeral’s type, such as coerce (x: RadixPointNumera
whose body reads the four numbers. A numeral at a place whose type is a type of a program’s own that declares no
coercion from the numeral’s type is a static error: coercion does not chain (Section 17.1), so the numeral is not con-
verted into its default first. The coercion sees the four numbers of a numeral as written: a negative constant reaches it
as the prefix operator − applied to the coercion’s result for the natural numeral (Section 13.27), so a type without that
operator refuses it. At each place where such a numeral stands, the coercion is applied once, not at each evaluation of
the place, so that the numeral there denotes one object, as a string literal does: two evaluations of one place yield the
same object, and two places yield two objects. A numeral type is written in a program only as the type of a parameter,

                                                           125
                           of a coercion or of an operator, never as the type of a variable, a field or a functional’s result, nor as a static argument;
                          so the constants pi and e of the Fortress standard libraries are values of R64 . Inside the body of a coercion, two
                          values of a numeral type are equal, and strictly equivalent, when their values v/rm are equal: there 2.5 and 2.50 are
                          strictly equivalent, and so are 0.12 and 0.5 .

                            R EVISED BY THE 2026 REVIVAL    SEE Section I.1.50

                            The Working Draft of February 2011 said that numerals are not directly converted to any of the number types, and so gave a
                            numeral where nothing fixes a type its own type. The revival decided on 8 November 2026 that a numeral is converted where
                            it stands: where its place fixes a type, into that type, and elsewhere into the default above; that a type of a program’s own
                            receives a numeral only through its coercion from the numeral’s type, once for each place; and that the numeral types are
                            written only as parameter types. The text this replaces, the revival’s own of 29 September 2026 (Section I.1.37), named the
                            type of an integer numeral IntLiteral, the name that the compiled path’s own library gives it.

What is an “integer”
in this context?
Not if the second in-
                          In Fortress, dividing two integers using the / operator produces a rational number; this is true regardless of whether
teger is 0.               the integers are of type Z (or ZZ), Z64 (or ZZ64), N32 (or NN32), or whatever. Addition, subtraction, multiplication,
                          and division of rationals are always exact; thus values such as 1/3 are represented exactly in Fortress.

                            D RAFT NOTE
                            We should give an example with a radix specifier.

# Rung T: the specification of the numeral types, their conversion and default, the fold, and a string literal as one object (rung-literals-spec)

- problem: the specification still gave a numeral the type `IntLiteral`, said that walk gives it `ZZ32` until it runs the checker and that numerals are not directly converted, and said nothing of the default, the fold's result or a string literal's identity (`Specification/basic/expressions/literals.tex:132-165` at b430f9f428; `basic/conversions-coercions.tex:74-90`; `basic/inference.tex:183-187`, `:299-317`), against P-173, P-174, P-76, P-172 and P-171 (`explorations/coordinator/CLIMB-BATCH-29.md:613-617`)
- spec: `Specification-1.0-frozen/basic/expressions/literals.tex:83-148` (the Working Draft's numeral types and "Numerals are not directly converted"), the governing passage this rung revises; `Specification/basic/expressions/literals.tex:98-235` after the change
- precedent: the revision form of Appendix I's latest entry, "The conversions between the integer types" (`Specification/appendices/changes.tex:4890-4961` at b430f9f428), and climb batch 28's rung V, whose specification change put its reasoning in its report and wrote no decision record (`explorations/compile-ladder/rung-integer-conversions/REPORT.md:1`)
- deviation: no `decision-record.md` (`fortress-repo`'s `specification.md`, part 4): the brief's section asks for none and allows nothing else under `explorations/`, so this report holds the full reasoning, and the new entries cite it (`Specification/appendices/changes.tex:5110-5113`)
- deviation: the section title "A Numeral Whose Conversions Tie" is kept over a section now wider than ties, since ledger rows and rung N's fork N6 cite it by title (`Specification/basic/inference.tex:302`)
- historical: `Specification/advanced-lib/binary.tex`, `Specification/appendices/changes.tex`, `Specification/basic-lib/numbers.tex`, `Specification/basic/conversions-coercions.tex`, `Specification/basic/expressions/constant.tex`, `Specification/basic/expressions/literals.tex`, `Specification/basic/inference.tex`, `Specification/basic/objects.tex`, `Specification/basic/trait-parameters.tex` (each present at `a874948ac`; `Specification/basic/expressions/literals.tex:1`)

Commit on `wip/rung-literals-spec`: fcf9b18219 (the specification, 9 files, +844 −106). The worktree was seeded by `seed-worktree.sh` (exit 0, 3 s).

## What changed and why

The decided design (P-173, P-174, P-76, P-172, P-171, P-165, P-40) is written into the specification in the revision form (P-96), with two new Appendix I entries and four revised. T writes the decided design, not the rungs' code (fork T3); the rungs' forks whose behaviour the text states are N1-N12, C1-C8, F1-F8 and S1-S2 (`CLIMB-BATCH-29.md:347-395`).

Passage by passage (the full reasoning P-96 asks for; each original is quoted in the entry named):

1. **A string literal, one object** (`Specification/basic/expressions/literals.tex:72-86`, box `:83` to `revival-string-literals`). New: two literals of one text denote one object; a string built at run time is another object unless the operation answers an existing string; strings stay reference objects; a concatenation of literals is a literal. Reason: P-171. Original: none (the Draft is silent; `Specification-1.0-frozen/basic/expressions/literals.tex:57` stands). Way back: each evaluation constructs a new string.
2. **The numeral types** (`literals.tex:98-118`, `:134-150`, box `:139` to `revival-numerals`). New: `Numeral` comprises `NaturalNumeral` and `RadixPointNumeral`; the four numbers `n`, `m`, `r`, `v` are fields, the getters `digits`, `fractionDigits`, `radix`, `digitValue` (`ZZ32`, `ZZ32`, `ZZ32`, `ZZ`); the explicit-radix types fold into the radix, `Literal[\v\]` into the digit count; the team's two draft notes stand and the box answers them. Reason: P-174, fork N1, N3; the judgement's "Changed in form: `:83-129`" (`reviews/literal-design-judgement-2026-11-08.md:24-29`). Original: `Specification-1.0-frozen/basic/expressions/literals.tex:83-86`, `:104-129`. Way back: static parameters again, which no library can declare.
3. **"Numerals are not directly converted"** (`literals.tex:156-163` rewritten; `:164-171` the Draft's `:141-148` kept as written). New: a numeral is converted where it stands, into the type its place fixes, and not before. Reason: P-173; the judgement keeps `:141-148` and contradicts `:132-141` at places that fix no type. Original: `Specification-1.0-frozen/basic/expressions/literals.tex:132-141`, quoted in `revival-numerals`.
4. **The conversion and the default** (`literals.tex:172-235`, box `:230`, replacing the box `revival-numeral-type` of `:149-165` at b430f9f428). New: each of the eight number types coerces from `NaturalNumeral`, `QQ`, `RR64`, `RR32` from `RadixPointNumeral`, exact or one rounding; a place fixes a type when its declared type declares a coercion from the numeral's type or is a numeral type; the places named; the default `ZZ32`, `ZZ64` or `ZZ` by value, `RR64` with a radix point, at an untyped binding, `Any`, `Object`, `Number`, a type parameter without a bound; out of range or rounding to an infinity a static error (fork C3); the default for a numeral only, never an expression of a numeral type; a program's type through its own coercion, refused without one (no chain, fork C4), seeing the four numbers as written, a negative constant through prefix `-` (fork C6), applied once per place, one object per place; a numeral type written only as a parameter type (fork C2), so `pi` and `e` are `RR64`; inside a coercion's body equal and `SEQV` by `v/r^m` (fork N9). Reason: P-173, P-174, P-76, P-172. Way back: in the `revival-numerals` Rationale.
5. **Static rational expressions** (`literals.tex:239-274`, kept, box `:268`): the fold on both paths, `x = 7/2` a `QQ`, `1/2 = 0.5`, at most one rounding. Reason: P-173, F1, F3.
6. **The constant traits and the fold** (`Specification/basic/expressions/constant.tex:80-110`, box `:101`). The Draft's list of trait groups stands; new paragraph: `library` declares no constant trait; an expression of numerals and operators folds exactly into a signed constant, its forms (F1), its three defaults, the operators left alone (F2). Reason: P-173 and the judgement's repair 3; "Changed in form: `constant.tex:44-74`". Original: `Specification-1.0-frozen/basic/expressions/constant.tex:44-56`, quoted. Way back: constant traits declared with static arguments.
7. **The two concatenations** (`constant.tex:113-133`, boxes `:121` to `revival-string-literals` and `:128` to `revival-numerals`): kept, now built (S1, F4). Original: `Specification-1.0-frozen/basic/expressions/constant.tex:75-82`, which stands.
8. **The coercions of the number types** (`Specification/basic-lib/numbers.tex:40-69`, box `:62`): `QQ`, `RR64`, `RR32` from both numeral types, the integer types from `NaturalNumeral`, exact or one rounding, each with its `=` pair (N8), `asFloat` on both numeral types (P-165, fork N4). The original is the revival's own text (`numbers.tex:43` at b430f9f428), quoted in `revival-numerals`.
9. **The box on integers in floating-point expressions** (`Specification/basic/conversions-coercions.tex:84-88`, inside the box `revival-int-float`): `NaturalNumeral` for `IntLiteral`; the checker against the one library and walk convert an integer numeral at `RR64` whatever its value; the sentence on the prelude stands. Original: the revival's own `conversions-coercions.tex:84-88`, quoted.
10. **The default beside coercion** (`conversions-coercions.tex:105-125`, box `:119`): the default is not a coercion; a numeral is applicable without coercion to a parameter of its default type and to one that fixes no type, its conversion into any other type a coercion, so `h(5)` takes `h(x: ZZ32)` over `h(x: Any)` (C4, P-49); a program's type without the coercion refuses it. The Draft's `conversions-coercions.tex:78-81` stands (the judgement's "Changed in form: `:98-101`").
11. **`id(3)`** (`Specification/basic/inference.tex:183-190`, box `:188`): instantiated at the default `ZZ32`, the result coerced (C1).
12. **The numeral section widened** (`inference.tex:305-350`, box `:345`): the default at every place that fixes no type, the receiver whose member the default declares (C1), the narrowest default for a type parameter that several numerals fix (`pick(3, 3000000000)` at `ZZ64`, `<|3000000000, 0.5|>` a `List[\RR64\]`) and for the branches of an `if` or `case` at an untyped binding, the float tie read `RR64`, `round(2.50000000000000001)` 2 (P-172, N12).

14. **A `nat` parameter used as a value** (`Specification/basic/trait-parameters.tex:105-113`): the text stands; the box says that a `nat` used as a value is a `ZZ32` (P-40, P-173, C5) and quotes what it contradicts by pointing to the entry (fork T2).

16. **Appendix I** (`Specification/appendices/changes.tex`): the new entries `revival-numerals` (`:4983-5333`) and `revival-string-literals` (`:5335-5411`), before "Passages not yet revised"; the entries `revival-numeral-type`, `revival-inference`, `revival-asfloat` and `revival-object-kinds` revised (below). ## Revival change

**The change.** The Working Draft of February 2011 gives a numeral the types `NaturalNumeral[\n,10,v\]`, `RadixPointNumeral[\n,m,10,v\]`, their explicit-radix variants, `Literal[\v\]` and `Numeral[\n,m,r,v\]`, whose static arguments are the digit count, the digits after the radix point, the radix and the value, and says that "Numerals are not directly converted to any of the number types because, as in common mathematical usage, we expect them to be polymorphic" (`Specification-1.0-frozen/basic/expressions/literals.tex:83-141`); it says nothing of whether two string literals of one text are one object, and that a `nat` parameter "may ... appear in any context that a variable of type NN32 can appear" (`Specification-1.0-frozen/basic/trait-parameters.tex:83-86`). # Rung T: the specification of the numeral types, their conversion and default, the fold, and a string literal as one object (rung-literals-spec)

- problem: the specification still gave a numeral the type `IntLiteral`, said that walk gives it `ZZ32` until it runs the checker and that numerals are not directly converted, and said nothing of the default, the fold's result or a string literal's identity (`Specification/basic/expressions/literals.tex:132-165` at b430f9f428; `basic/conversions-coercions.tex:74-90`; `basic/inference.tex:183-187`, `:299-317`), against P-173, P-174, P-76, P-172 and P-171 (`explorations/coordinator/CLIMB-BATCH-29.md:613-617`)
- spec: `Specification-1.0-frozen/basic/expressions/literals.tex:83-148` (the Working Draft's numeral types and "Numerals are not directly converted"), the governing passage this rung revises; `Specification/basic/expressions/literals.tex:98-235` after the change
- precedent: the revision form of Appendix I's latest entry, "The conversions between the integer types" (`Specification/appendices/changes.tex:4890-4961` at b430f9f428), and climb batch 28's rung V, whose specification change put its reasoning in its report and wrote no decision record (`explorations/compile-ladder/rung-integer-conversions/REPORT.md:1`)
- deviation: no `decision-record.md` (`fortress-repo`'s `specification.md`, part 4): the brief's section asks for none and allows nothing else under `explorations/`, so this report holds the full reasoning, and the new entries cite it (`Specification/appendices/changes.tex:5111-5114`)
- deviation: the section title "A Numeral Whose Conversions Tie" is kept over a section now wider than ties, since ledger rows and rung N's fork N6 cite it by title (`Specification/basic/inference.tex:302`)
- historical: `Specification/advanced-lib/binary.tex`, `Specification/appendices/changes.tex`, `Specification/basic-lib/numbers.tex`, `Specification/basic/conversions-coercions.tex`, `Specification/basic/expressions/constant.tex`, `Specification/basic/expressions/literals.tex`, `Specification/basic/inference.tex`, `Specification/basic/objects.tex`, `Specification/basic/trait-parameters.tex` (each present at `a874948ac`; `Specification/basic/expressions/literals.tex:1`)

Commit on `wip/rung-literals-spec`: fcf9b18219 (the specification, 9 files, +844 −106). The worktree was seeded by `seed-worktree.sh` (exit 0, 3 s).

## What changed and why

The decided design (P-173, P-174, P-76, P-172, P-171, P-165, P-40) is written into the specification in the revision form (P-96), with two new Appendix I entries and four revised. T writes the decided design, not the rungs' code (fork T3); the rungs' forks whose behaviour the text states are N1-N12, C1-C8, F1-F8 and S1-S2 (`CLIMB-BATCH-29.md:347-395`).

Passage by passage (the full reasoning P-96 asks for; each original is quoted in the entry named):

1. **A string literal, one object** (`Specification/basic/expressions/literals.tex:72-86`, box `:83` to `revival-string-literals`). New: two literals of one text denote one object; a string built at run time is another object unless the operation answers an existing string; strings stay reference objects; a concatenation of literals is a literal. Reason: P-171. Original: none (the Draft is silent; `Specification-1.0-frozen/basic/expressions/literals.tex:57` stands). Way back: each evaluation constructs a new string.
2. **The numeral types** (`literals.tex:98-118`, `:134-150`, box `:139` to `revival-numerals`). New: `Numeral` comprises `NaturalNumeral` and `RadixPointNumeral`; the four numbers `n`, `m`, `r`, `v` are fields, the getters `digits`, `fractionDigits`, `radix`, `digitValue` (`ZZ32`, `ZZ32`, `ZZ32`, `ZZ`); the explicit-radix types fold into the radix, `Literal[\v\]` into the digit count; the team's two draft notes stand and the box answers them. Reason: P-174, fork N1, N3; the judgement's "Changed in form: `:83-129`" (`reviews/literal-design-judgement-2026-11-08.md:24-29`). Original: `Specification-1.0-frozen/basic/expressions/literals.tex:83-86`, `:104-129`. Way back: static parameters again, which no library can declare.
3. **"Numerals are not directly converted"** (`literals.tex:156-163` rewritten; `:164-171` the Draft's `:141-148` kept as written). New: a numeral is converted where it stands, into the type its place fixes, and not before. Reason: P-173; the judgement keeps `:141-148` and contradicts `:132-141` at places that fix no type. Original: `Specification-1.0-frozen/basic/expressions/literals.tex:132-141`, quoted in `revival-numerals`.
4. **The conversion and the default** (`literals.tex:172-235`, box `:230`, replacing the box `revival-numeral-type` of `:149-165` at b430f9f428). New: each of the eight number types coerces from `NaturalNumeral`, `QQ`, `RR64`, `RR32` from `RadixPointNumeral`, exact or one rounding; a place fixes a type when its declared type declares a coercion from the numeral's type or is a numeral type; the places named; the default `ZZ32`, `ZZ64` or `ZZ` by value, `RR64` with a radix point, at an untyped binding, `Any`, `Object`, `Number`, a type parameter without a bound; out of range or rounding to an infinity a static error (fork C3); the default for a numeral only, never an expression of a numeral type; a program's type through its own coercion, refused without one (no chain, fork C4), seeing the four numbers as written, a negative constant through prefix `-` (fork C6), applied once per place, one object per place; a numeral type written only as a parameter type (fork C2), so `pi` and `e` are `RR64`; inside a coercion's body equal and `SEQV` by `v/r^m` (fork N9). Reason: P-173, P-174, P-76, P-172. Way back: in the `revival-numerals` Rationale.
5. **Static rational expressions** (`literals.tex:239-274`, kept, box `:268`): the fold on both paths, `x = 7/2` a `QQ`, `1/2 = 0.5`, at most one rounding. Reason: P-173, F1, F3.
6. **The constant traits and the fold** (`Specification/basic/expressions/constant.tex:80-110`, box `:101`). The Draft's list of trait groups stands; new paragraph: `library` declares no constant trait; an expression of numerals and operators folds exactly into a signed constant, its forms (F1), its three defaults, the operators left alone (F2). Reason: P-173 and the judgement's repair 3; "Changed in form: `constant.tex:44-74`". Original: `Specification-1.0-frozen/basic/expressions/constant.tex:44-56`, quoted. Way back: constant traits declared with static arguments.
7. **The two concatenations** (`constant.tex:113-133`, boxes `:121` to `revival-string-literals` and `:128` to `revival-numerals`): kept, now built (S1, F4). Original: `Specification-1.0-frozen/basic/expressions/constant.tex:75-82`, which stands.
8. **The coercions of the number types** (`Specification/basic-lib/numbers.tex:40-69`, box `:62`): `QQ`, `RR64`, `RR32` from both numeral types, the integer types from `NaturalNumeral`, exact or one rounding, each with its `=` pair (N8), `asFloat` on both numeral types (P-165, fork N4). The original is the revival's own text (`numbers.tex:43` at b430f9f428), quoted in `revival-numerals`.
9. **The box on integers in floating-point expressions** (`Specification/basic/conversions-coercions.tex:84-88`, inside the box `revival-int-float`): `NaturalNumeral` for `IntLiteral`; the checker against the one library and walk convert an integer numeral at `RR64` whatever its value; the sentence on the prelude stands. Original: the revival's own `conversions-coercions.tex:84-88`, quoted.
10. **The default beside coercion** (`conversions-coercions.tex:105-124`, box `:119`): the default is not a coercion; a numeral is applicable without coercion to a parameter of its default type and to one that fixes no type, its conversion into any other type a coercion, so `h(5)` takes `h(x: ZZ32)` over `h(x: Any)` (C4, P-49); a program's type without the coercion refuses it. The Draft's `conversions-coercions.tex:78-81` stands (the judgement's "Changed in form: `:98-101`").
11. **`id(3)`** (`Specification/basic/inference.tex:183-190`, box `:188`): instantiated at the default `ZZ32`, the result coerced (C1).
12. **The numeral section widened** (`inference.tex:305-350`, box `:345`): the default at every place that fixes no type, the receiver whose member the default declares (C1), the narrowest default for a type parameter that several numerals fix (`pick(3, 3000000000)` at `ZZ64`, `<|3000000000, 0.5|>` a `List[\RR64\]`) and for the branches of an `if` or `case` at an untyped binding, the float tie read `RR64`, `round(2.50000000000000001)` 2 (P-172, N12).
13. **String literal, objects chapter** (`Specification/basic/objects.tex:66-74`, box `:71`): one sentence and a box (P-171).
14. **A `nat` parameter used as a value** (`Specification/basic/trait-parameters.tex:105-113`): the text stands; the box says that a `nat` used as a value is a `ZZ32` (P-40, P-173, C5) and quotes what it contradicts by pointing to the entry (fork T2).
15. **The binary chapter** (`Specification/advanced-lib/binary.tex:925`, `:1146`, `:1752`, `:1781`, `:1907`, `:2143`, `:2172`, `:2348`): eight boxes, one after each typeset group over `NaturalNumeral` (the Draft's `:905-914`, `:1117-1135`, `:1674-1735`, `:1750`, `:1860-1868`, `:2006-2099`, `:2114`, `:2271-2281`); the text stands (fork T2).
16. **Appendix I** (`Specification/appendices/changes.tex`): the new entries `revival-numerals` (`:4983-5333`) and `revival-string-literals` (`:5335-5411`), before "Passages not yet revised"; the entries `revival-numeral-type`, `revival-inference`, `revival-asfloat` and `revival-object-kinds` revised (below). The natives effect (`:4693-4694`, the base's `:4673-4674`) is the gather's (fork 4).

## Handover state line

- **T** (`<T>`): Rung T wrote P-173, P-174, P-76, P-172 and P-171 into the specification in the revision form: the literals chapter's `NaturalNumeral` and `RadixPointNumeral` below `Numeral` with the four numbers as fields, the conversion where a place fixes a type and the default elsewhere, a program's type through its coercion once per place; the constant chapter's fold and both concatenations built; the coercion chapter's default beside coercion; the inference chapter's numeral section widened; a string literal one object; eight binary-chapter callouts and one at `nat` parameters; Appendix I's `revival-numerals` and `revival-string-literals`, four entries revised; the build clean; NEW-T-1 (`=/=` at a numeral) and the `Index` place to the curator.

## Revival change

**The change.** The Working Draft of February 2011 gives a numeral the types `NaturalNumeral[\n,10,v\]`, `RadixPointNumeral[\n,m,10,v\]`, their explicit-radix variants, `Literal[\v\]` and `Numeral[\n,m,r,v\]`, whose static arguments are the digit count, the digits after the radix point, the radix and the value, and says that "Numerals are not directly converted to any of the number types because, as in common mathematical usage, we expect them to be polymorphic" (`Specification-1.0-frozen/basic/expressions/literals.tex:83-141`); it says nothing of whether two string literals of one text are one object, and that a `nat` parameter "may ... appear in any context that a variable of type NN32 can appear" (`Specification-1.0-frozen/basic/trait-parameters.tex:83-86`). The revised specification says that every numeral is a `Numeral`, a `NaturalNumeral` or a `RadixPointNumeral` with no static parameters, its four numbers fields of its value; that a numeral converts where it stands, into the type its place fixes (a type with a coercion from the numeral type, or a numeral type), exactly into the integer types and `QQ` and with one rounding into `RR64` and `RR32`, out of range a static error, and elsewhere into `ZZ32`, `ZZ64` or `ZZ` by its value, or `RR64` with a radix point; that an expression of numerals alone folds exactly into a signed constant with those defaults and `QQ` for a quotient; that a program's type receives a numeral only through its own coercion, once per place; that a numeral type is written only as a parameter type; that a `nat` used as a value is a `ZZ32`; and that two string literals of one text are one object, a concatenation of literals folded into one (`Specification/basic/expressions/literals.tex:72-235`; `constant.tex:80-133`; `inference.tex:305-350`; `trait-parameters.tex:105-113`; `objects.tex:66-74`). No test: an edit of the specification has none; the specification's build checks it, and the rungs' tests show the behaviour on the merged tree. The reason, as evidence: the Working Draft gives numerals types of their own so that "library designers [can] decide how numerals should interact with other types of objects by defining coercion operations" (`Specification-1.0-frozen/basic/expressions/literals.tex:141-145`), which the team built under the names `IntLiteral` and `FloatLiteral` with the exact value at the coercion ("ZZ32 now coerces IntLiteral as described in the spec", commit `128f313b5b`, 2009) but never with the four numbers; a coercion handed a double rounds twice where one rounding from the exact value gives the nearest value; and every team source that speaks of literals makes equal literals one value ("Literals are values; they do not require evaluation", `literals.tex:25-26`; "All literals represent value objects", `Documentation/Specification/Prose/Language/Expressions/literals.tick:29`; `ProjectFortress/compiler_regressions/seqv.fss:22`).

**Provenance.** P-173, P-174, P-76, P-172, P-171, P-165 and P-40; P-96 for the form; P-26, whose bend P-173's entry owns. The batch record's forks 1 to 8, T1 to T3, and the rungs' forks whose behaviour the text states (N1-N12, C1-C8, F1-F8, S1-S2). Climb batch 29, rung T.

# Rung T: the specification of the numeral types, their conversion and default, the fold, and a string literal as one object (rung-literals-spec)

- problem: the specification still gave a numeral the type `IntLiteral`, said that walk gives it `ZZ32` until it runs the checker and that numerals are not directly converted, and said nothing of the default, the fold's result or a string literal's identity (`Specification/basic/expressions/literals.tex:132-165` at b430f9f428; `basic/conversions-coercions.tex:74-90`; `basic/inference.tex:183-187`, `:299-317`), against P-173, P-174, P-76, P-172 and P-171 (`explorations/coordinator/CLIMB-BATCH-29.md:613-617`)
- spec: `Specification-1.0-frozen/basic/expressions/literals.tex:83-148` (the Working Draft's numeral types and "Numerals are not directly converted"), the governing passage this rung revises; `Specification/basic/expressions/literals.tex:98-235` after the change
- precedent: the revision form of Appendix I's latest entry, "The conversions between the integer types" (`Specification/appendices/changes.tex:4890-4961` at b430f9f428), and climb batch 28's rung V, whose specification change put its reasoning in its report and wrote no decision record (`explorations/compile-ladder/rung-integer-conversions/REPORT.md:1`)
- deviation: no `decision-record.md` (`fortress-repo`'s `specification.md`, part 4): the brief's section asks for none and allows nothing else under `explorations/`, so this report holds the full reasoning, and the new entries cite it (`Specification/appendices/changes.tex:5111-5114`)
- deviation: the section title "A Numeral Whose Conversions Tie" is kept over a section now wider than ties, since ledger rows and rung N's fork N6 cite it by title (`Specification/basic/inference.tex:302`)
- historical: `Specification/advanced-lib/binary.tex`, `Specification/appendices/changes.tex`, `Specification/basic-lib/numbers.tex`, `Specification/basic/conversions-coercions.tex`, `Specification/basic/expressions/constant.tex`, `Specification/basic/expressions/literals.tex`, `Specification/basic/inference.tex`, `Specification/basic/objects.tex`, `Specification/basic/trait-parameters.tex` (each present at `a874948ac`; `Specification/basic/expressions/literals.tex:1`)

Commit on `wip/rung-literals-spec`: fcf9b18219 (the specification, 9 files, +844 −106). The worktree was seeded by `seed-worktree.sh` (exit 0, 3 s).

## What changed and why

The decided design (P-173, P-174, P-76, P-172, P-171, P-165, P-40) is written into the specification in the revision form (P-96), with two new Appendix I entries and four revised. T writes the decided design, not the rungs' code (fork T3); the rungs' forks whose behaviour the text states are N1-N12, C1-C8, F1-F8 and S1-S2 (`CLIMB-BATCH-29.md:347-395`).

Passage by passage (the full reasoning P-96 asks for; each original is quoted in the entry named):

1. **A string literal, one object** (`Specification/basic/expressions/literals.tex:72-86`, box `:83` to `revival-string-literals`). New: two literals of one text denote one object; a string built at run time is another object unless the operation answers an existing string; strings stay reference objects; a concatenation of literals is a literal. Reason: P-171. Original: none (the Draft is silent; `Specification-1.0-frozen/basic/expressions/literals.tex:57` stands). Way back: each evaluation constructs a new string.
2. **The numeral types** (`literals.tex:98-118`, `:134-150`, box `:139` to `revival-numerals`). New: `Numeral` comprises `NaturalNumeral` and `RadixPointNumeral`; the four numbers `n`, `m`, `r`, `v` are fields, the getters `digits`, `fractionDigits`, `radix`, `digitValue` (`ZZ32`, `ZZ32`, `ZZ32`, `ZZ`); the explicit-radix types fold into the radix, `Literal[\v\]` into the digit count; the team's two draft notes stand and the box answers them. Reason: P-174, fork N1, N3; the judgement's "Changed in form: `:83-129`" (`reviews/literal-design-judgement-2026-11-08.md:24-29`). Original: `Specification-1.0-frozen/basic/expressions/literals.tex:83-86`, `:104-129`. Way back: static parameters again, which no library can declare.
3. **"Numerals are not directly converted"** (`literals.tex:156-163` rewritten; `:164-171` the Draft's `:141-148` kept as written). New: a numeral is converted where it stands, into the type its place fixes, and not before. Reason: P-173; the judgement keeps `:141-148` and contradicts `:132-141` at places that fix no type. Original: `Specification-1.0-frozen/basic/expressions/literals.tex:132-141`, quoted in `revival-numerals`.
4. **The conversion and the default** (`literals.tex:172-235`, box `:230`, replacing the box `revival-numeral-type` of `:149-165` at b430f9f428). New: each of the eight number types coerces from `NaturalNumeral`, `QQ`, `RR64`, `RR32` from `RadixPointNumeral`, exact or one rounding; a place fixes a type when its declared type declares a coercion from the numeral's type or is a numeral type; the places named; the default `ZZ32`, `ZZ64` or `ZZ` by value, `RR64` with a radix point, at an untyped binding, `Any`, `Object`, `Number`, a type parameter without a bound; out of range or rounding to an infinity a static error (fork C3); the default for a numeral only, never an expression of a numeral type; a program's type through its own coercion, refused without one (no chain, fork C4), seeing the four numbers as written, a negative constant through prefix `-` (fork C6), applied once per place, one object per place; a numeral type written only as a parameter type (fork C2), so `pi` and `e` are `RR64`; inside a coercion's body equal and `SEQV` by `v/r^m` (fork N9). Reason: P-173, P-174, P-76, P-172. Way back: in the `revival-numerals` Rationale.
5. **Static rational expressions** (`literals.tex:239-274`, kept, box `:268`): the fold on both paths, `x = 7/2` a `QQ`, `1/2 = 0.5`, at most one rounding. Reason: P-173, F1, F3.

Reason: P-173 and the judgement's repair 3; "Changed in form: `constant.tex:44-74`". Original: `Specification-1.0-frozen/basic/expressions/constant.tex:44-56`, quoted. The original is the revival's own text (`numbers.tex:43` at b430f9f428), quoted in `revival-numerals`.
9. **The box on integers in floating-point expressions** (`Specification/basic/conversions-coercions.tex:84-88`, inside the box `revival-int-float`): `NaturalNumeral` for `IntLiteral`; the checker against the one library and walk convert an integer numeral at `RR64` whatever its value; the sentence on the prelude stands. Original: the revival's own `conversions-coercions.tex:84-88`, quoted.
10. **The default beside coercion** (`conversions-coercions.tex:105-124`, box `:119`): the default is not a coercion; a numeral is applicable without coercion to a parameter of its default type and to one that fixes no type, its conversion into any other type a coercion, so `h(5)` takes `h(x: ZZ32)` over `h(x: Any)` (C4, P-49); a program's type without the coercion refuses it. The Draft's `conversions-coercions.tex:78-81` stands (the judgement's "Changed in form: `:98-101`").
11. **`id(3)`** (`Specification/basic/inference.tex:183-190`, box `:188`): instantiated at the default `ZZ32`, the result coerced (C1).
12. **The numeral section widened** (`inference.tex:305-350`, box `:345`): the default at every place that fixes no type, the receiver whose member the default declares (C1), the narrowest default for a type parameter that several numerals fix (`pick(3, 3000000000)` at `ZZ64`, `<|3000000000, 0.5|>` a `List[\RR64\]`) and for the branches of an `if` or `case` at an untyped binding, the float tie read `RR64`, `round(2.50000000000000001)` 2 (P-172, N12).

14. **A `nat` parameter used as a value** (`Specification/basic/trait-parameters.tex:105-113`): the text stands; the box says that a `nat` used as a value is a `ZZ32` (P-40, P-173, C5) and quotes what it contradicts by pointing to the entry (fork T2).

The revised specification says that every numeral is a `Numeral`, a `NaturalNumeral` or a `RadixPointNumeral` with no static parameters, its four numbers fields of its value; that a numeral converts where it stands, into the type its place fixes (a type with a coercion from the numeral type, or a numeral type), exactly into the integer types and `QQ` and with one rounding into `RR64` and `RR32`, out of range a static error, and elsewhere into `ZZ32`, `ZZ64` or `ZZ` by its value, or `RR64` with a radix point; that an expression of numerals alone folds exactly into a signed constant with those defaults and `QQ` for a quotient; that a program's type receives a numeral only through its own coercion, once per place; that a numeral type is written only as a parameter type; that a `nat` used as a value is a `ZZ32`; and that two string literals of one text are one object, a concatenation of literals folded into one (`Specification/basic/expressions/literals.tex:72-235`; `constant.tex:80-133`; `inference.tex:305-350`; `trait-parameters.tex:105-113`; `objects.tex:66-74`). No test: an edit of the specification has none; the specification's build checks it, and the rungs' tests show the behaviour on the merged tree. The reason, as evidence: the Working Draft gives numerals types of their own so that "library designers [can] decide how numerals should interact with other types of objects by defining coercion operations" (`Specification-1.0-frozen/basic/expressions/literals.tex:141-145`), which the team built under the names `IntLiteral` and `FloatLiteral` with the exact value at the coercion ("ZZ32 now coerces IntLiteral as described in the spec", commit `128f313b5b`, 2009) but never with the four numbers; a coercion handed a double rounds twice where one rounding from the exact value gives the nearest value; and every team source that speaks of literals makes equal literals one value ("Literals are values; they do not require evaluation", `literals.tex:25-26`; "All literals represent value objects", `Documentation/Specification/Prose/Language/Expressions/literals.tick:29`; `ProjectFortress/compiler_regressions/seqv.fss:22`).
